subject: bayesplot: plot grouped by experimental conditions (aka predictors)

messages.author: 6e49ac0768ace996
messages.subject: bayesplot: plot grouped by experimental conditions (aka predictors)
parts:
Hi,

I wondered if it is possible to plot different posterior predictive checks based on the value of the predictor variable using bayesplot.
Consider the following regression model in 'brms':

    brm(y ~ condition + (1 | subject))

I know that I can produce different plots on each group level (which corresponds to 'subject' in the formula above if I got this correct).
But I didn't find an option to produce plots based on the levels of the 'condition' variable, which is of more interest to me as I want to see how different the predictions are for the different experimental conditions (collapsing across subjects).

Is there such option yet, is this not possible, or am I just too blind to find it?

Best,
Thomas

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: bayesplot: plot grouped by experimental conditions (aka predictors)
parts:
Hi Thomas, if 'condition' is discrete then there's no problem just using that variable instead of 'subject' as the group. The 'group' argument to any bayesplot function that ends in '_grouped' allows you to use any variable that splits the data into groups, regardless of how you use that variable in your model. I don't know if brms allows you to specify that in its interface to bayesplot (I would think so, but I'm not sure), but it's definitely possible with bayesplot. 

In addition, several of the ppc functions in bayesplot (e.g. ppc_intervals) also take an 'x' argument, which is typically for continuous predictors, but could also be used if 'condition' is an integer.

Jonah
